text:
Victor Eklund is riding a five-game point streak (four goals, two assists) and has seven goals in 19 games, a lot for a 20-year-old rookie the Islanders took 16th overall in 2025. He has earned a few more minutes along the way, up to 15:16 a night over his last ten. The New York Post wrote this week about Brayden Schenn taking him under his wing, and Mason Marchment was fined for roughing him, which tells you opponents have noticed him too.

Now the caution. He's shooting 24.1%, roughly double the league norm, and the Islanders have scored 9.7 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. His own chances are fine for his role (4.77 expected goals, a measure of shot quality), but the goals are running well ahead of them. At five-on-five the Isles get just under half the expected goals in his minutes. None of that makes the start fake; it means the scoring pace probably cools even if his game keeps growing. Forwards drafted where he was have scored a median 0.32 points a game in their first full season. He's well past that, and that's the real story.
